17/// A dictionary, which is a key-value map, keys being names, and values being any PDF object or
18/// objetc reference.
19#[derive(Clone)]
20pub struct Dict<'a>(Inner<'a>);
21
22#[derive(Clone)]
23enum Inner<'a> {
24    Empty,
25    Some(Arc<Repr<'a>>),
26}
27
28impl Default for Dict<'_> {
29    fn default() -> Self {
30        Self::empty()
31    }
32}
33
34// Note that this is not structural equality, i.e. two dictionaries with the same
35// items are still considered different if they have different whitespaces.
36impl PartialEq for Dict<'_> {
37    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
38        self.data() == other.data()
39    }
40}
41
42impl<'a> Dict<'a> {
43    /// Create a new empty dictionary.
44    pub fn empty() -> Self {
45        Self(Inner::Empty)
46    }
47
48    /// Get the raw bytes underlying to the dictionary.
49    pub fn data(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
50        match &self.0 {
51            Inner::Empty => &[],
52            Inner::Some(repr) => repr.data,
53        }
54    }
55
56    /// Returns the number of entries in the dictionary.
57    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
58        self.offsets().map_or(0, FxHashMap::len)
59    }
60
61    /// Return whether the dictionary is empty.
62    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
63        self.offsets().is_none_or(FxHashMap::is_empty)
64    }
65
66    /// Checks whether the dictionary contains an entry with a specific key.
67    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> bool {
68        self.offsets().is_some_and(|offsets| offsets.contains_key(key.as_ref()))
69    }
70
71    /// Returns the entry of a key as a specific object, or try to resolve it in case it's
72    /// an object reference.
73    #[allow(private_bounds, reason = "users shouldn't be able to implement `ObjectLike` for custom objects.")]
74    pub fn get<T>(&self, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Option<T>
75    where
76        T: ObjectLike<'a>,
77    {
78        self.get_raw::<T>(key.as_ref())?.resolve(self.ctx())
79    }
80
81    /// Get the object reference linked to a key.
82    pub fn get_ref(&self, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Option<ObjRef> {
83        let offset = *self.offsets()?.get(key.as_ref())?;
84
85        Reader::new(&self.data()[offset..]).read_with_context::<ObjRef>(self.ctx())
86    }
87
88    /// Returns an iterator over all keys in the dictionary.
89    pub fn keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Name<'a>> + '_ {
90        self.offsets().into_iter().flat_map(|offsets| offsets.keys().cloned())
91    }
92
93    /// An iterator over all entries in the dictionary, sorted by key.
94    pub fn entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (Name<'a>, MaybeRef<Object<'a>>)> + '_ {
95        let mut sorted_keys = self.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>();
96        sorted_keys.sort_by(|n1, n2| n1.as_ref().cmp(n2.as_ref()));
97        sorted_keys.into_iter().map(|k| {
98            let obj = self.get_raw(k.deref()).unwrap();
99            (k, obj)
100        })
101    }
102
103    /// Return the object identifier of the dict, if it's an indirect object.
104    pub fn obj_id(&self) -> Option<ObjectIdentifier> {
105        self.ctx().obj_number()
106    }
107
108    /// Return the raw entry for a specific key.
109    #[allow(private_bounds)]
110    pub fn get_raw<T>(&self, key: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Option<MaybeRef<T>>
111    where
112        T: Readable<'a>,
113    {
114        let offset = *self.offsets()?.get(key.as_ref())?;
115
116        Reader::new(&self.data()[offset..]).read_with_context::<MaybeRef<T>>(self.ctx())
117    }
118
119    pub(crate) fn ctx(&self) -> &ReaderContext<'a> {
120        match &self.0 {
121            Inner::Empty => ReaderContext::dummy_ref(),
122            Inner::Some(repr) => &repr.ctx,
123        }
124    }
125
126    fn offsets(&self) -> Option<&FxHashMap<Name<'static>, usize>> {
127        match &self.0 {
128            Inner::Empty => None,
129            Inner::Some(repr) => Some(repr.offsets.get_or_init(|| {
130                // PdfCraft patch: (#307) large resource dictionaries are read for every
131                // page at open, but most are never looked up. Index them only on demand.
132                // The first pass already validated the same immutable bytes with this
133                // context. Keep the same parser, including duplicate-key and repair rules.
134                let mut offsets = new_offsets();
135                let mut reader = Reader::new(repr.data);
136                let (start, end): (Option<&[u8]>, &[u8]) = if repr.inline { (None, b"ID") } else { (Some(b"<<"), b">>") };
137                let _ = parse_dict_with(&mut reader, &repr.ctx, start, end, |name, offset, _| {
138                    offsets.insert(name.into_owned(), offset);
139                    Some(())
140                });
141                offsets
142            })),
143        }
144    }
145}

147impl Debug for Dict<'_> {
148    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
149        let mut debug_struct = f.debug_struct("Dict");
150
151        if let Some(offsets) = self.offsets() {
152            let mut r = Reader::new(self.data());
153
154            for (key, val) in offsets {
155                r.jump(*val);
156                debug_struct.field(&format!("{:?}", key.as_str()), &r.read_with_context::<MaybeRef<Object<'_>>>(&ReaderContext::dummy()).unwrap());
157            }
158        }
159        Ok(())
160    }
161}

163impl Skippable for Dict<'_> {
164    fn skip(r: &mut Reader<'_>, is_content_stream: bool) -> Option<()> {
165        r.forward_tag(b"<<")?;
166        r.enter_container()?;
167
168        // PdfCraft patch: leave even when a value or garbage fails through `?`.
169        let result = (|| loop {
170            r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
171
172            if let Some(()) = r.forward_tag(b">>") {
173                break Some(());
174            } else {
175                let Some(_) = r.skip::<Name<'_>>(is_content_stream) else {
176                    // In case there is garbage in-between, be lenient and just try to skip it.
177                    r.skip::<Object<'_>>(is_content_stream)?;
178                    continue;
179                };
180
181                r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
182
183                if is_content_stream {
184                    r.skip::<Object<'_>>(is_content_stream)?;
185                } else {
186                    r.skip::<MaybeRef<Object<'_>>>(is_content_stream)?;
187                }
188            }
189        })();
190        r.leave_container();
191        result
192    }
193}

195impl<'a> Readable<'a> for Dict<'a> {
196    fn read(r: &mut Reader<'a>, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<Self> {
197        read_inner(r, ctx, Some(b"<<"), b">>")
198    }

201// PdfCraft patch: (#307) retain the fast single-pass index for ordinary small
202// dictionaries. Above this entry count, validate without retaining a hash table.
203const EAGER_DICT_ENTRIES: usize = 32;
204
205fn new_offsets() -> FxHashMap<Name<'static>, usize> {
206    return FxHashMap::with_capacity_and_hasher(8, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher);
207    #[cfg(any())]
208    FxHashMap::new()
209}
210
211pub(crate) type SharedIndex = Arc<OnceLock<FxHashMap<Name<'static>, usize>>>;
212
213#[derive(Debug)]
214pub(crate) struct CachedDict {
215    data: Box<[u8]>,
216    offsets: SharedIndex,
217}
218
219// PdfCraft patch: share a validated large dictionary's index across pages. The cache
220// belongs to the xref, owns its keys, and is bounded even on documents with many unique
221// dictionaries. Comparing the bytes also makes address reuse harmless. No reader context
222// is cached: decryption, object identity and reference-cycle tracking stay with each read.
223#[derive(Debug, Default)]
224pub(crate) struct DictCache {
225    entries: FxHashMap<usize, Arc<CachedDict>>,
226    bytes: usize,
227}
228
229impl DictCache {
230    fn get(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Option<Arc<CachedDict>> {
231        self.entries.get(&(data.as_ptr() as usize)).filter(|cached| data.starts_with(&cached.data)).cloned()
232    }
233
234    fn insert(&mut self, data: &[u8], offsets: SharedIndex) {
235        const MAX_BYTES: usize = 8 << 20;
236        if self.entries.len() < 256 && data.len() <= MAX_BYTES.saturating_sub(self.bytes) {
237            self.bytes += data.len();
238            self.entries.insert(data.as_ptr() as usize, Arc::new(CachedDict { data: data.into(), offsets }));
239        }
240    }
241}
242
243fn read_inner<'a>(r: &mut Reader<'a>, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>, start_tag: Option<&[u8]>, end_tag: &[u8]) -> Option<Dict<'a>> {
244    let cacheable = start_tag.is_some() && !ctx.in_content_stream();
245    if cacheable {
246        let tail = r.tail()?;
247        if let Some(cached) = ctx.xref().with_dict_cache(|cache| cache.get(tail)).flatten() {
248            let data = r.read_bytes(cached.data.len())?;
249            return Some(Dict(Inner::Some(Arc::new(Repr { data, offsets: cached.offsets.clone(), inline: false, ctx: ctx.clone() }))));
250        }
251    }
252    let mut offsets = Some(new_offsets());
253
254    let (data, repaired) = parse_dict_with(
255        r,
256        ctx,
257        start_tag,
258        end_tag,
259        #[inline]
260        |name, offset, _| {
261            if let Some(index) = &mut offsets {
262                index.insert(name.into_owned(), offset);
263                if index.len() > EAGER_DICT_ENTRIES {
264                    offsets = None;
265                }
266            }
267            Some(())
268        },
269    )?;
270
271    let index = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
272    if let Some(offsets) = offsets {
273        let _ = index.set(offsets);
274    }
275    // Repair may read objects through the current reference context; only cache the
276    // context-independent validating path. Inline/content dictionaries stay uncached.
277    if cacheable && !repaired && data.len() >= 1024 {
278        ctx.xref().with_dict_cache(|cache| cache.insert(data, index.clone()));
279    }
280    Some(Dict(Inner::Some(Arc::new(Repr { data, offsets: index, inline: start_tag.is_none(), ctx: ctx.clone() }))))
281}

283pub(crate) struct DictProbe<'a> {
284    pub(crate) data: &'a [u8],
285    pub(crate) has_root: bool,
286    pub(crate) has_type: bool,
287}
288
289// We use that method during fallback xref parsing, so that we can search for
290// the dictionaries we need without allocating the whole hash map.
291// If the above TODOs are ever resolved, we can probably remove this method.
292pub(crate) fn probe_dict<'a>(r: &mut Reader<'a>, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>, start_tag: Option<&[u8]>, end_tag: &[u8]) -> Option<DictProbe<'a>> {
293    let mut has_root = false;
294    let mut has_type = false;
295
296    let (data, _) = parse_dict_with(
297        r,
298        ctx,
299        start_tag,
300        end_tag,
301        #[inline]
302        |name, _, _value_reader| {
303            if name.as_ref() == keys::ROOT {
304                has_root = true;
305            } else if name.as_ref() == keys::TYPE {
306                has_type = true;
307            }
308
309            Some(())
310        },
311    )?;
312
313    Some(DictProbe { data, has_root, has_type })
314}
315
316// PdfCraft patch: an object where a key belongs is read, not skipped, so a dictionary
317// holding another one there (`<< << …`) recursed without a bound. Count each parsed
318// dictionary like a skipped one, and leave on every exit of the parse below.
319fn parse_dict_with<'a, F>(
320    r: &mut Reader<'a>,
321    ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>,
322    start_tag: Option<&[u8]>,
323    end_tag: &[u8],
324    on_entry: F,
325) -> Option<(&'a [u8], bool)>
326where
327    F: FnMut(Name<'a>, usize, &Reader<'a>) -> Option<()>,
328{
329    r.enter_container()?;
330    let result = parse_dict_with_inner(r, ctx, start_tag, end_tag, on_entry);
331    r.leave_container();
332    result
333}
334
335fn parse_dict_with_inner<'a, F>(
336    r: &mut Reader<'a>,
337    ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>,
338    start_tag: Option<&[u8]>,
339    end_tag: &[u8],
340    mut on_entry: F,
341) -> Option<(&'a [u8], bool)>
342where
343    F: FnMut(Name<'a>, usize, &Reader<'a>) -> Option<()>,
344{
345    let dict_data = r.tail()?;
346    let start_offset = r.offset();
347    let mut repaired = false;
348
349    // Inline image dictionaries don't start with '<<'.
350    if let Some(start_tag) = start_tag {
351        r.forward_tag(start_tag)?;
352    }
353
354    loop {
355        r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
356
357        // Normal dictionaries end with '>>', inline image dictionaries end with BD.
358        if let Some(()) = r.peek_tag(end_tag) {
359            r.forward_tag(end_tag)?;
360            let end_offset = r.offset() - start_offset;
361
362            break Some((&dict_data[..end_offset], repaired));
363        } else {
364            let Some(name) = r.read_without_context::<Name<'_>>() else {
365                if start_tag.is_some() {
366                    // In case there is garbage in-between, be lenient and just try to skip it.
367                    // But only do this if we are parsing a proper dictionary as opposed to an
368                    // inline dictionary.
369                    repaired = true;
370                    r.read::<Object<'_>>(ctx)?;
371                    continue;
372                } else {
373                    return None;
374                }
375            };
376            r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
377
378            let offset = r.offset() - start_offset;
379            // Do note that we are including objects in our dictionary even if they
380            // are the null object, meaning that a call to `contains_key` will return `true`
381            // even if the object is the null object. The PDF reference in theory requires
382            // us to treat them as non-existing. Previously, we included a check to determine
383            // whether the object is `null` before inserting it, but that caused problems
384            // in some test cases where encryption + object streams are involved (as we would
385            // attempt to read an object stream before having resolved the encryption dictionary).
386            on_entry(name, offset, r)?;
387
388            if ctx.in_content_stream() {
389                r.skip::<Object<'_>>(ctx.in_content_stream())?;
390            } else {
391                r.skip::<MaybeRef<Object<'_>>>(ctx.in_content_stream())?;
392            }
393        }
394    }
395}

420#[cfg(any())]
421mod lazy_index_tests {
422    use super::*;
423    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::{Array, FromBytes};
424    use alloc::string::String;
425
426    fn entries() -> String {
427        let mut data = String::new();
428        for i in 0..100 {
429            data.push_str(&format!("/Key{i} {i} "));
430        }
431        // Escaped and long names, duplicate keys, null and nested values keep
432        // exactly the same semantics after the second (index-building) pass.
433        data.push_str("/Key99 123 /Esc#61ped 7 /ThisNameIsLongerThanTheInlineNameBuffer 9 /Nil null /Nested << /N [1 2 3] >> ");
434        data
435    }
436
437    #[cfg(any())]
438    fn large_indexes_are_deferred_and_clones_share_the_result() {
439        let data = format!("<< {} >>", entries());
440        let dict = Dict::from_bytes(data.as_bytes()).unwrap();
441        let Inner::Some(repr) = &dict.0 else { panic!("nonempty") };
442        assert!(repr.offsets.get().is_none());
443        let cloned = dict.clone();
444        assert_eq!(cloned.get::<i32>(b"Key99"), Some(123));
445        assert!(repr.offsets.get().is_some());
446        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 104);
447        assert_eq!(dict.get::<i32>(b"Escaped"), Some(7));
448        assert_eq!(dict.get::<i32>(b"ThisNameIsLongerThanTheInlineNameBuffer"), Some(9));
449        assert!(dict.contains_key(b"Nil"));
450        assert!(!dict.contains_key(b"Missing"));
451        assert_eq!(dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(b"Nested").unwrap().get::<Array<'_>>(b"N").unwrap().iter::<i32>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [1, 2, 3]);
452        assert_eq!(dict.keys().count(), dict.len());
453        assert_eq!(dict.entries().count(), dict.len());
454        assert!(core::ptr::eq(dict.offsets().unwrap(), cloned.offsets().unwrap()));
455    }
456
457    #[cfg(any())]
458    fn small_indexes_stay_eager_and_large_inline_dicts_work() {
459        let dict = Dict::from_bytes(b"<< /Key 42 >>").unwrap();
460        let Inner::Some(repr) = &dict.0 else { panic!("nonempty") };
461        assert!(repr.offsets.get().is_some());
462        assert_eq!(dict.get::<i32>(b"Key"), Some(42));
463        let data = format!("{} ID", entries());
464        let mut reader = Reader::new(data.as_bytes());
465        let inline = InlineImageDict::read(&mut reader, &ReaderContext::dummy()).unwrap();
466        assert_eq!(inline.0.get::<i32>(b"Key99"), Some(123));
467        assert_eq!(inline.0.len(), 104);
468    }
469
470    #[cfg(any())]
471    fn large_dicts_are_still_validated_before_any_lookup() {
472        let data = format!("<< {} /Broken [", entries());
473        assert!(Dict::from_bytes(data.as_bytes()).is_none());
474    }
475
476    #[cfg(any())]
477    fn repeated_resource_reads_share_indexes_but_keep_object_context() {
478        let data = format!(
479            "%PDF-1.7\n1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj\n2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R 4 0 R] /Count 2 >> endobj\n3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 100 100] /Resources 5 0 R >> endobj\n4 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 100 100] /Resources 5 0 R >> endobj\n5 0 obj << /XObject << {} >> >> endobj\ntrailer << /Root 1 0 R >>\n%%EOF",
480            entries()
481        );
482        let pdf = crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf::new(data.into_bytes()).unwrap();
483        let a = pdf.xref().get::<Dict<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)).unwrap().get::<Dict<'_>>(b"XObject").unwrap();
484        let b = pdf.xref().get::<Dict<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)).unwrap().get::<Dict<'_>>(b"XObject").unwrap();
485        let (Inner::Some(a_repr), Inner::Some(b_repr)) = (&a.0, &b.0) else { panic!("nonempty") };
486        assert!(Arc::ptr_eq(&a_repr.offsets, &b_repr.offsets));
487        assert_eq!(a.obj_id(), Some(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)));
488        assert_eq!(a.get::<i32>(b"Key99"), Some(123));
489        assert_eq!(b.get::<i32>(b"Escaped"), Some(7));
490        assert!(core::ptr::eq(a.offsets().unwrap(), b.offsets().unwrap()));
491    }
492
493    #[cfg(any())]
494    fn index_cache_is_bounded_and_rejects_changed_or_truncated_bytes() {
495        let mut cache = DictCache::default();
496        let mut data = format!("<< {} >>", entries()).into_bytes();
497        cache.insert(&data, Arc::new(OnceLock::new()));
498        assert!(cache.get(&data).is_some());
499        assert!(cache.get(&data[..data.len() - 1]).is_none());
500        data[3] = b'Z';
501        assert!(cache.get(&data).is_none());
502        let buffers: Vec<_> = (0..300).map(|i| format!("<< /Key{i} 1 >>").into_bytes()).collect();
503        for data in &buffers {
504            cache.insert(data, Arc::new(OnceLock::new()));
505        }
506        assert_eq!(cache.entries.len(), 256);
507        assert!(cache.bytes <= 8 << 20);
508    }
509}

511/// A collection of possible keys in a PDF dictionary. Copied and adapted from `PDFBox`.
512#[allow(missing_docs)]
513pub mod keys {
514    macro_rules! key {
515        ($i:ident, $e:expr) => {
516            pub const $i: &'static [u8] = $e;
517        };
518    }

1164#[cfg(any())]
1165mod tests {
1166    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::Number;
1167    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::dict::keys::{COLORSPACE, EXT_G_STATE, FONT, PROC_SET};
1168    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::dict::{Dict, InlineImageDict};
1169    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::string;
1170    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::{Name, ObjRef};
1171    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::reader::Reader;
1172    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::reader::{ReaderContext, ReaderExt};
1173
1174    fn dict_impl(data: &[u8]) -> Option<Dict<'_>> {
1175        Reader::new(data).read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::dummy())
1176    }
1177
1178    #[cfg(any())]
1179    fn empty_dict_1() {
1180        let dict_data = b"<<>>";
1181        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1182
1183        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 0);
1184    }
1185
1186    #[cfg(any())]
1187    fn empty_dict_2() {
1188        let dict_data = b"<<   \n >>";
1189        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1190
1191        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 0);
1192    }
1193
1194    #[cfg(any())]
1195    fn dict_1() {
1196        let dict_data = b"<<  /Hi 34.0 >>";
1197        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1198
1199        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 1);
1200        assert!(dict.get::<Number>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Hi")).is_some());
1201    }
1202
1203    #[cfg(any())]
1204    fn dict_2() {
1205        let dict_data = b"<<  /Hi \n 34.0 /Second true >>";
1206        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1207
1208        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 2);
1209        assert!(dict.get::<Number>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Hi")).is_some());
1210        assert!(dict.get::<bool>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Second")).is_some());
1211    }
1212
1213    #[cfg(any())]
1214    fn dict_complex() {
1215        let data = "<< /Type /Example
1216/Subtype /DictionaryExample
1217/Version 0.01
1218/IntegerItem 12
1219/StringItem ( a string )
1220/Subdictionary << /Item1 0.4
1221                /Item2 true
1222                /LastItem ( not ! )
1223                /VeryLastItem ( OK )
1224                >>
1225>>";
1226
1227        let dict = Reader::new(data.as_bytes()).read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::dummy()).unwrap();
1228        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 6);
1229        assert!(dict.get::<Name<'_>>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Type")).is_some());
1230        assert!(dict.get::<Name<'_>>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Subtype")).is_some());
1231        assert!(dict.get::<Number>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Version")).is_some());
1232        assert!(dict.get::<i32>(Name::new_unescaped(b"IntegerItem")).is_some());
1233        assert!(dict.get::<string::String<'_>>(Name::new_unescaped(b"StringItem")).is_some());
1234        assert!(dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(Name::new_unescaped(b"Subdictionary")).is_some());
1235    }
1236
1237    #[cfg(any())]
1238    fn dict_with_trailing() {
1239        let dict_data = b"<<  /Hi 67.0  >>trailing data";
1240        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1241
1242        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 1);
1243    }
1244
1245    #[cfg(any())]
1246    fn dict_with_comment() {
1247        let dict_data = b"<<  /Hi % A comment \n 67.0 % Another comment \n >>";
1248        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1249
1250        assert_eq!(dict.len(), 1);
1251    }
1252
1253    #[cfg(any())]
1254    fn inline_dict() {
1255        let dict_data = b"/W 17 /H 17 /CS /RGB /BPC 8 /F [ /A85 /LZW ] ID ";
1256
1257        let dict = Reader::new(&dict_data[..]).read_with_context::<InlineImageDict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::dummy()).unwrap();
1258
1259        assert_eq!(dict.get_dict().len(), 5);
1260    }
1261
1262    #[cfg(any())]
1263    fn dict_with_escaped_name() {
1264        let dict_data = b"<< /PANTONE#20104#20C 234 >>";
1265        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1266
1267        assert!(dict.contains_key("PANTONE 104 C"));
1268    }
1269
1270    #[cfg(any())]
1271    fn garbage_in_between() {
1272        let dict_data = b"<< 
1273/ProcSet [ /PDF /Text ] 
1274/Font << /F4 31 0 R /F6 23 0 R >> 
1275/ExtGState << /GS2 14 0 R
12762000
1277 /GS3 15 0 R >> 
1278/ColorSpace << /Cs5 13 0 R >> 
1279>> ";
1280        let dict = dict_impl(dict_data).unwrap();
1281
1282        assert!(dict.contains_key(PROC_SET));
1283        assert!(dict.contains_key(FONT));
1284        assert!(dict.contains_key(EXT_G_STATE));
1285        assert!(dict.contains_key(COLORSPACE));
1286
1287        let Some(dict) = dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(EXT_G_STATE) else {
1288            panic!("failed to parse ext g state");
1289        };
1290
1291        assert_eq!(dict.get_ref("GS2"), Some(ObjRef::new(14, 0)));
1292        assert_eq!(dict.get_ref("GS3"), Some(ObjRef::new(15, 0)));
1293    }
1294}
